text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the offload RFC — I sketched an alternative where we split the offload API into two orthogonal surfaces: 1) lifecycle (pin/unpin/migrate/evict) and 2) accounting/usage (acct-token, residency-report). The goal is to let the runtime manage residency without leaking allocator internals.
ken: Interesting. How would callers get notified about eviction ordering? We still need a predictable contract for eviction callbacks for low-latency code paths.
alex: We should avoid synchronous callbacks on the hot path. Suggest an async event + ordered sequence number. Callers can opt-in to sync notifications where they can take the perf hit.
maria: Right — proposal: keep a tiny sync API (try_pin/try_unpin) that returns success/fail immediate. For eviction order awareness, emit small ordered events to a per-tenant event queue and surface via pollable fd for private deployments.
rachel: For Dedicated we also need clear billing signals. If accounting is separate, we can charge per-residency-second via acct-token ties to allocation id.
infra-bot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled for offload-api-shim v0.1 to staging at 03:00 UTC :rocket: 
samir: Two pull requests we need: (1) ABI shim that maps existing allocator calls to lifecycle+acct calls, (2) runtime changes that implement async ordered events. I'll own the shim.
ken: Edge case: what about pinned mappings where the model expects stable device pointers? We need a 'hard pin' path that blocks or migrates synchronously with a bounded timeout.
alex: Agree — expose hard_pin(timeout_ms) and document OOM behaviour. Also add a 'soft_unmap' that unmaps on GPU side but keeps accounting metadata.
maria: Telemetry: add tracer fields: residency_start, residency_score, evict_reason, acct_token. We can use these for Optimize to recommend quant levels.
rachel: SLA implications: if hard_pin fails under pressure, fallback plan should be model fallback (lower-quality variant) + alerting. Add rollout knob to enforce fallback at 90th percentile.
samir: Implementation note: avoid embedding allocator internals in acct-token; that's a leaky abstraction. acct-token should be opaque string; the runtime maps it to internal records.
ken: Ops ask: make the event queue size configurable per-tenant and expose backpressure metrics. We don't want tenants to block core threads.
maria: Ok action items: ken -> design hard_pin semantics doc; samir -> RFC PR for shim and owners; alex -> event queue sketch + perf model; rachel -> billing mapping for acct-token; I'll collate into a new RFC draft by EOD Wednesday.
rachel: +1. also add a short example snippet for customers showing soft_unmap vs hard_pin.
alex: Example sketch:
```
// keep stable ptr when possible
if (runtime.hard_pin(id, 50 /*ms*/)) {
  use_gpu_ptr(id);
} else {
  fallback_to_cpu_variant();
}
```
maria: Thanks all. We'll discuss in next arch sync if anyone wants to push back. :thumbsup:
